notes.summary: Exact-source audit: saved BFJ 1201.0188v1 retains function-field algebraizability and SNC support; BE 1805.01016v3 is the norms paper and reports only a descent/resolution-restricted characteristic-p envelope result. Ten source hashes verified.
notes.detailedSummary: The original characteristic-zero proof uses cofinal regular SNC models, skeleton equicontinuity, multiplier-ideal positivity and envelope regularization, then bounded/unbounded locality and algebraizability-dependent orthogonality. The saved 1201.0188 is actual v1, not a later unrestricted theorem. Its algebraizability concerns descent of X to a one-variable function field with completion K; L need not descend. BE's reported positive-characteristic envelope result instead assumes descent of (X,L) to a function field of transcendence degree d and resolution in dimension n+d. This report neither covers mixed characteristic nor supplies a full finite-energy equation theorem. All ten supplied PDF/text hashes and six abstract hashes match; originals and literal proof extracts were preserved.
notes.text:
The source audit uses only input.json, the ten expressly listed public caches, and newly created workspace artifacts.

BFJ, arXiv:1201.0187v2, assumes complete discrete valuation, residue characteristic zero, smooth projective X and ample L. Its banner is 21 January 2014; its internal manuscript date is 22 October 2018. SNC cofinality enters the original psh definition and retractions. Sections 5–8 also use multiplier ideals for positivity, toroidal equicontinuity for normalized compactness, and subadditivity/global generation/vanishing for envelope continuity and regularization. Resolving a model alone does not replace these ideal-theoretic uses.

The actual saved arXiv:1201.0188v1 has banner 30 December 2011. Theorem A requires a smooth projective X over complete discretely valued K of residue characteristic zero, ample L, and a positive Radon measure of mass (L^n) supported on an SNC dual complex. X must be algebraizable in the precise sense X=Y_K for smooth projective Y over a one-variable function field F whose completion is K. The statement does not require L to descend. Appendix A uses that algebraizability to prove orthogonality via compactification and big-line-bundle decompositions. The operator/locality construction also depends on the companion characteristic-zero approximation theory. This saved theorem cannot be cited as a later arbitrary-support theorem.

ArXiv:1805.01016v3, banner 8 January 2021, is Boucksom–Eriksson, Spaces of norms, determinant of cohomology and Fekete points in non-Archimedean geometry. Theorem 9.15 gives relative volume = relative MA energy for continuous psh metrics on a semiample Q-line bundle on geometrically reduced projective X over any complete valued field. Smooth X and ample L meet those hypotheses. Section 7.30 still labels unrestricted envelope continuity conjectural. It reports the discrete characteristic-p result with (X,L) descending to a function field of transcendence degree d and resolution assumed in dimension n+d, using test ideals. The cited GJKM paper is not supplied, so its exact stronger resolution formulation is not independently reconstructed here. The report gives no mixed-characteristic conclusion and no unbounded equation theorem in this draft.

Pille–Schneider 2209.04879v2, Remark 4.4, distinguishes defining E1 from extending MA to E1. Section 1.2 expressly assumes equicharacteristic zero; the shorter wording “characteristic zero” in the remark does not establish a mixed-characteristic endpoint.

Execution evidence: python3 source_audit.py reported 10 verified sources, 20 matching PDF/text SHA256 values, six matching abstract hashes, byte_identical_input=true and 52 literal excerpts. notes.summary: Published partial theorem: in positive characteristic with trivial valuation, smooth connected projective X has the genuine E1 operator in every dimension; arbitrary-support finite-dual-energy measures have unique solutions when dim X≤2. This does not solve the nontrivial residue-characteristic axis.
notes.detailedSummary: Apply Boucksom–Jonsson 1801.08229v4 over algebraically closed trivially valued k of characteristic p>0, smooth connected projective X, and ample L. The reference is the canonical trivial metric and raw mass V=(L^n). The exact condition is sup_H{V E(u)−∫u dμ}<∞, equivalently V E∨(μ/V)<∞, with μ(Xan)=V. The finite-energy pairing defines a unique positive Riesz measure extending model MA; decreasing-net continuity proves approximation independence. Locality/comparison and injectivity hold in every dimension. The positive-characteristic envelope proof resolves test configurations of dimension n+1, and uses test ideals; its unconditional dimension range is n≤2. Envelope compactness plus the energy bound and L1 continuity give an actual maximizer, and energy differentiation proves its MA equation. For n≥3 surjectivity is conditional on the envelope property, which is not proved here.
notes.text:
This is an application of the published Boucksom–Jonsson theorem in arXiv:1801.08229v4, not a new solution of P16.3.

Hypotheses: k is algebraically closed of characteristic p>0 with trivial absolute value; X/k is smooth, connected and projective, dimension n≥1; L is ample. Fix its canonical trivial reference metric ρ, write ω=c1(L) and V=(L^n)>0. PSH(L) consists of nontrivial usc decreasing limits of Fubini–Study functions u=m^{-1}max_i(log|s_i|+λ_i), with basepoint-free sections of mL and rational λ_i. The weak topology is pointwise convergence on divisorial valuations. The energy is E(u)=(ω,u)^{n+1}/((n+1)V), extended monotonically, and E1={E>−∞}. The raw energy is V E. For continuous semipositive u it equals (n+1)^{-1}Σ_{j=0}^n∫u(ω+dd^c u)^j∧ω^{n−j}.

The measure condition is positivity, raw mass μ(Xan)=V, and
E*raw_ρ(μ)=sup_{u∈H(L)}[V E(u)−∫u dμ]<∞.
For ν=μ/V this is exactly V E∨(ν). It also equals the supremum over E1. Indeed, if u_j∈H decreases to u∈E1, then E(u_j)→E(u), while ∫u_j dν≥E(u_j)−E∨(ν). Monotone integration of usc functions on compact Xan gives ∫u_j dν→∫u dν, with finite limit by the displayed lower bound. Thus u∈L1(ν), and its energy expression is the limit of model expressions. Conversely H⊂E1. Constant tests yield c(V−μ(Xan)); rational constants already show that finite raw dual energy forces the exact mass V. No restricted measure is renormalized.

Operator construction: use the finite-energy multilinear pairing of Theorem 7.14, whose monotone extension and mixed-energy bounds are published inputs. For PL f, T_u(f)=(0,f)·(ω,u)^n is positive (Theorem 7.18), T_u(1)=V, and |T_u(f)|≤V||f||∞. PL is uniformly dense in C0 (Theorem 2.2), so Riesz gives a unique positive Radon measure MAraw_ρ(u). Pairing continuity makes T_{u_j}(f) converge for every decreasing model approximation of u; density and the uniform bound give convergence on all continuous tests. The result is independent of the approximating net. Proposition 7.19 identifies it with the model intersection measure Σ_F b_F((ω_𝓧+D)|_F)^n δ_{v_F}, proves raw mass V and finite-energy integrability. Theorem A gives strong continuity and dense image in finite-energy measures, in every dimension.

Locality is Theorem 7.40 on the Borel sets {u>v}. Applying it to max(u,v−ε) and using mass V yields
∫_{u<v−ε}MAraw(v)≤∫_{u≤v−ε}MAraw(u).
The infinite loci are null by finite-energy integrability. Letting ε↓0 gives the comparison inequality ∫_{u<v}MAraw(v)≤∫_{u<v}MAraw(u). If MA(u)=MA(v), then I(u,v)=∫(u−v)(MA(v)−MA(u))=0. Corollary 10.4, using divisorial energy estimates and divisorial determination, implies u−v locally constant. Connectedness gives one constant. This proves injectivity in every dimension.

For n≤2, Theorem 5.20 proves the envelope property in characteristic p. It reduces continuous obstacles to PL ones and identifies envelopes through normalized base ideals on a test configuration. Resolution is applied to the total test configuration of dimension n+1≤3, then test ideals replace characteristic-zero multiplier ideals in the subadditivity/global-generation estimate. That estimate forces uniform convergence of nef approximants. These resolution/test-ideal results are background used by the published theorem, not new unrestricted resolution claims. Actual PDF page 62 visibly distinguishes dim X≤2 from dim 𝓧≤3; page 63 states the test-ideal replacement.

The envelope property implies normalized weak compactness (Theorem 5.11). For a finite-energy ν, take a maximizing sequence for Fν(u)=E(u)−∫u dν, normalized to sup u=0. Lemma 9.15/Corollary 9.16 bound J(u)=sup u−E(u). Compactness gives a convergent subnet; upper semicontinuity of E gives a finite-energy limit u. Proposition 9.19 gives L1(ν) convergence, so Fν(u)≥limsup Fν(u_j)=E∨(ν). Thus u actually attains the supremum.

Theorem 8.5 gives E↓(u+tf)=E(u)+t∫f MA(u)+O(t²) for PL f, uniformly in u; Corollary 8.6 handles continuous tests. With the envelope property E↓ is the energy of the psh envelope. For a maximizing family with defect δ_j→0 this yields
t∫f MA(u_j)≤t∫f dν+δ_j+C_f t².
First let j tend to the limit, then t↓0, and repeat with −f. The constant maximizing sequence u_j=u proves MA(u)=ν, hence MAraw(u)=μ. This is Theorem 12.8's variational proof and Theorem 12.9's positive-characteristic n≤2 conclusion.

Therefore arbitrary-support finite-dual-energy measures have unique finite-energy solutions on smooth projective curves and surfaces over this trivially valued k. No continuity of the solution is asserted. In dimensions ≥3 the operator, comparison and injectivity remain established, while surjectivity is conditional on the envelope property. The theorem does not apply to arbitrary varieties over F_p((t)) or Q_p: their valuation is nontrivial, and Q_p has characteristic zero but positive residue characteristic.

Full cited argument and proof boundaries: P16.3-argument.md, Section 3, and standalone P16.3-paper.tex. Actual PDF page checks and literal proofs are in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. Rerun artifact generation/build: python3 build_and_check.py.

notes.summary: Full P16.3 remains unresolved here: arbitrary-field continuous/test MA and synthetic orthogonality/measure density do not construct the unbounded operator or an actual solution potential. Deliverables are saved; both final TeX passes succeeded.
notes.detailedSummary: For smooth projective X and ample L over genuinely nontrivially discretely valued K with positive residue characteristic, BE supplies continuous genuine MA and BJ 2307.01697v1 supplies test orthogonality and strong approximation of finite-energy measures without a residue-characteristic restriction. The latter explicitly does not investigate finite-energy potentials; its completed measure space is not identified with E1/R. Recent CLD and Gubler–Rabinoff local theories do not supply the missing global implication. Six concrete obligations remain: singular psh compactness, envelope/model positivity replacements, genuine unbounded mixed MA, exact dual-energy/differentiation passages, actual arbitrary-support solution potentials, and unbounded comparison/injectivity. The 12-page paper and exact status schema were produced; source/input checks and successful compilation are execution evidence only.
